newsitem.title: CANADA: PanCanadian daily output seen below plan.
newsitem.headline: PanCanadian daily output seen below plan.

text.p: PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd said on Wednesday its 1996 average daily crude oil output would be below forecasts, but would be fairly close to the target it set at the beginning of the year.
The company also said increasing crude oil production volume would occupy its attention in the final quarter.

"We have lagged slightly in our production growth target due to weather related problems and equipment delays in bringing new production onstream. These issues are now resolved," David Tuer, president and chief executive, said in a statement.

"Our daily average production for 1996 will be below our initial expectations, but with Canadian conventional crude production growing to 133,000 barrels per day by year-end, we will be very close to the aggressive target we set in January," he added.

PanCanadian said it reaped substantial rewards from higher world oil prices. The company has hedged about 50 percent of its 1996 crude oil production at an average price of US$18.45 per barrel. The remaining 50 percent is sold at prevailing world prices.
